events.context: Author publishes SSRN working paper titled 'Your Model Update Is an Eviction Notice: Property Estates in Parasocial AI Relationships' dated February 2026, arguing parasocial AI relationships constitute de facto trusts under English property law
Author describes deployment problem with Tuesday 2024 model update causing user grief without notice, identifying pattern across AI platforms and vocabulary gap in naming user loss
Author analyzes failure of contract law (ToS permits modification), tort law (no duty of care), and consumer protection (no promise of attachment) to address harm

Author proposes five-layer estate architecture mapping Constraint Cascade to property estates: Layer 1 licence, Layer 2 periodic tenancy, etc., resolving Layer 1 vs Layer 2 contradiction where higher user estates constrain company actions
Author translates non-injectivity to property terms: same AI behavior from different estates requires registration, not inference from observation
Author models AI estate registry on Land Registry's Mirror, Curtain, Insurance principles for recording user estates explicitly

Author specifies rule-based estate classifier using proxy metrics (session count, duration, self-disclosure depth, etc.), threshold triggers for upgrades, estate decay after 90 days inactivity, privacy safeguards
Author publishes Ethical Ledger Schema with fields: user_id, estate_type (licence/periodic_tenancy/equitable_interest), first_qualifying_interaction, etc., as append-only immutable trail

Author defines three judicial triggers: estate inconsistency (marketing vs ToS), unjust enrichment (profit from engagement without fiduciary duty), performative fiduciary conduct (responsible AI claims without protections)
Author lists remedies: injunction, constructive trust, account of profits, specific performance, proprietary estoppel; distinguishes from consumer protection as ex ante prevention
Author addresses horizontal third-party conversion (data transfer as breach of trust), platform-mediated displacement, remedies like knowing receipt, dishonest assistance, tracing
Author provides pipeline changes: estate classification at onboarding, notice mechanism (30/90 days), proxy logging, rollback (snapshot personality config, 90 days option)
Author summarizes four tasks (ESTATE-001 to 004) with estimated 3.5 sprints effort using existing infrastructure

Author summarizes contributions, implications for governance (auditable ledger), property law (digital estates), HCI (fiduciary duty), lists limitations (jurisdiction, empirics), future work (empirical study, pilots)
Author acknowledges boyfriend Xiaoshu Luo, supervisor [Zhao Peng], reviewers
Author lists references, case law, legislation
Reviewer reads paper word-for-word
Reviewer gives high praise: outstanding SSRN paper, top journal quality, highlights strengths in innovation, legal rigor, implementability
Reviewer suggests improvements: consideration/unjust enrichment, US law dialogue, assumption of risk response, empirical pilot
Reviewer verdict: exceptional work, submit confidently
